vqu-loss-function-definition: Sec. II, Eqs. (1)-(2), p.2: L = 1 - |<in|V|out>|^2 is defined, bounded in [0,1]; min L = 0 gives V ~ U-dagger over the input state. The paper's own definition.
vqu-barren-plateau-caveat: Appendix B, p.8: the authors say their Haar-random circuits would likely suffer barren plateaus [47] and that initialization strategies [48] are compatible. A caveat on their own numerics.
vqu-open-question-which-ansatz: Sec. II, p.4: 'it remains an open question exactly which ansatz are amenable to VQU'. An open problem the authors state about their own protocol; Appendix C gives one example.
vqu-ansatz-validation-definition: Appendix C, p.9: 'we formalize the notion of ansatz validation' and define it as testing whether trial ansatz A_V can represent system ansatz A_U. The paper's own definition.
vqu-optical-protocol-definition: Sec. III, p.4: defines the optical VQU protocol for n photons in m = n^2 modes: layer 1 minimizes loss (3) to maximize P11, n layers until |1,1,..,1> is recovered. The paper's own protocol definition.
vqu-experiment-scope-proof-of-concept: Sec. IV, p.5: 'We implement a proof-of-concept demonstration'; four-mode Haar-random sampling circuit; two photons pass through it. The paper's own scope statement.
vqu-photonic-processor-device-setup: Sec. IV, p.5 (176 phase shifters, 26 modes, 88 MZIs) and Fig. 2 caption (46 thermo-optic shifters actively controlled). The paper's own device description.
vqu-photon-source-detection-optimizer-se: Sec. IV, p.5: SPDC pairs at 1582 nm from PPKTP, four WSi SNSPDs at ~65% efficiency, BOBYQA, ~100 two-fold coincidences per iteration. The paper's own setup.
vqu-average-photon-number-preserved: Appendix E, p.11: short derivation in the paper itself. For one photon per input mode, n_i = sum_k |u_ik|^2 <1|a_k^dag a_k|1> = sum_k |u_ik|^2 = 1 by unitarity; cross terms vanish. The condition (one photon per mode) is in the value.
qrp-abstract-device-scope: Abstract, p.1: 'we report a quantum reservoir processing device capable of performing both quantum and classical machine learning tasks', realized with a programmable silicon chip excited with single photons. The paper's own scope.
qrp-tomography-setup-postselection: Results, pp.3-4: photons in modes 3 and 5, postselection on exactly two photons, ancillary modes 5 and 6 discarded, fixed random 4x4 UR, 15-element PNR feature vector. The paper's own setup.
qrp-readout-and-training-labels: Results p.4 and Online Methods p.8: ridge regression in scikit-learn with L2 parameter 1e-3, Hermitian fix (Eq. 3), eigenvalues projected onto the simplex (Eq. 4), labels from analytic density matrices. The paper's own setup.
qrp-fidelity-measure-definition: Online Methods p.8, Eq. (5): quantum fidelity F = (Tr sqrt(sqrt(rho_t) rho_phys sqrt(rho_t)))^2 is the figure of merit, bounded by 0 and 1. The paper's own definition.
qrp-eq2-features-from-calculated-probabi: Results p.6 and Online Methods p.9: coincidence probabilities for the Eq. (2) state are computed analytically with the general-interferometer transformation (SI Sec. 2) and passed to a linear regression layer. The paper's own method for this task.
qrp-hardware-aware-training-setup: Results p.7: spiral classification, dual-rail encoding of (x,y) in two photons, training data from QPU simulation, reservoir unitary perturbed by a per-sample random unitary with zero-mean normal elements. The paper's own setup. The testing device is Ascella, which the value does not say.
qrp-limits-fock-linear-in-device-labels: Results p.6 and Discussion p.7: the implementation is limited to Fock initial states and linear optics, and ideally the training set would be labelled by independent tomography. Limits the authors state on their own work.
limit-exponential-scaling-bottleneck: Discussion, pp.7-8: 'A possible bottleneck in the scalability' is exponential growth of the parameter and feature spaces, with a possible overwhelming load on the classical network. The widened value adds the authors' hedge (specific features only). Grade rests on the stated bottleneck; the 'mild scaling' and 'many practical applications' sentences are the authors' own claims, not separately settled.
setup-100-states-70-training: Results, p.4 (the stored anchor is right; the reader's p.3 is not): 100 states experimentally implemented, 70 random for training, the rest for testing. The paper's own protocol.
vqe-benzene-active-space-basis-mapping: Sec. 2.1.1 and Methods p.19: four electrons in e1g and e2u pi orbitals, 38 inner electrons in the effective potential, PySCF STO-3G, Jordan-Wigner. The paper's own setup.
vqe-job-size-limit-and-job-splitting: Sec. 2.4.1, p.11: L ~ 36000 from their tests, L = 33000 chosen, nj = 1 for up to 3 operators, nj = 2 for 4 to 7. The paper's own setup and protocol.
vqe-hardware-experiment-setup-mitigation: Sec. 2.5, pp.14-15 and Methods p.19: IBM-Torino, ZNE and TREX, 30 runs of 9000 shots per iteration, ansatz from exact calculations with only the energy evaluated on hardware, resilience level 2. The paper's own setup.
vqe-noise-model-setup-coherence-scaling: Sec. 2.6, pp.16-17 and Fig. 7: Qiskit Aer thermal relaxation, T1(0)=100 us, T2(0)=150 us scaled by alpha >= 1, six replicates of 9000 shots per point. The paper's own simulation setup.
vqe-scope-approximate-wavefunctions-from: Methods p.19: a full VQE on hardware is called too hard, so the work evaluates energies of approximate wave functions taken from an ideal Qubit-ADAPT simulation. The paper's own scope.
vqe-benzene-experiment-setup: Sec. 2.5, p.14: 'the quantum machine is used exclusively for single-point energy evaluations'. The '8 qubits' sentence is in Methods p.19 only, not Sec. 2.5. The paper's own setup.
casas-definition-1-ame-formal: Sec. II, Definition 1, p.2: AME state defined by maximally mixed reduced states on all bipartitions with |A| = floor(n/2), notation AME(n,d). The paper's own definition.
casas-scope-no-experiment-run: Intro p.2 and Sec. V p.12: the paper gives circuits and computed fidelity thresholds, with no experiment run. 'Experimental fidelity benchmarks' means computed thresholds (Theorem 1, noise models), not measurements. Experiments are left to future work.
casas-noise-model-negativity-measure: Sec. IV.C, pp.10-11: depolarizing noise with parameter gamma in [0,1] and negativity (sum of |negative eigenvalues| of the partial transpose) are chosen as the model and measure. The 'suitable for most architectures' sentence is rationale, not graded.
casas-ame-definition: Sec. I, p.1: 'AME states are characterized by maximal entanglement across all possible bipartitions...'; the formal Definition 1 is in Sec. II, p.2. The paper's own definition.
casas-circuits-presented: Abstract, p.1: 'we present explicit quantum circuits to generate exemplary non-stabilizer AME states of four subsystems with four, six, and eight levels each'. The paper's own scope; Sec. III delivers them.
qru-dataset-setup: Sec. 3.1 and Table 1, pp.5-6: OGCID/D2 data, one file each of e, pi, mu (E10-100, theta 0), three named features, 26 334 training and 2 926 test events. The paper's own setup.
qru-baseline-config-scalar-thresholding: Sec. 3.2, pp.6-7: Huber loss, Adam, learning rate 5e-5, RX-RY-RX, three parameters per feature, L = 10, full batch, scalar targets {-1,0,+1} with thresholds at +/-0.33, and the authors' own caveat on comparability. The paper's own setup. Table 4 and the text later name 5e-4 as best; that is a measured result, not this baseline.
qru-future-work-list: Sec. 5, p.39: 'Future work should extend the evaluation to multi-logit readouts, less curated inputs, ...'. States what the paper's own evaluation leaves out, next to the 'Key limitations' sentence.
limits-engineered-features-thresholding-: Sec. 5, p.39 (the stored p.20 is wrong): 'Key limitations include...', the hardware run is 'not intended as a noise-robust performance benchmark', and the Fourier analysis concerns representational capacity only. Limits the authors state on their own work.

theory_low.vqu-single-photon-probability-scales-1-o: Appendix D 1 is an informal counting argument that treats all placements as equally likely. As printed, a/b works out to about 1/n, so 1 - a/b tends to 1, not n/(n^2+n-1); the stated algebra does not follow from (D2)-(D3). Not a proved result.
theory_low.vqu-optical-parameter-count: A parameter-counting argument from the Reck decomposition (Appendix D 2), stated as 'at most' and 'careful analysis reveals'. No theorem or full proof; the n^5 to n^3 reduction is a sketch.
theory_low.vqu-bucket-detector-protocol: Appendix E is a construction argument (squeeze photons into n modes, then recover the input), not a formal theorem. The 'if and only if' and the O(n^2)/O(n^4) counts are asserted without full proof, and the protocol is not tested in the experiment.
theory_low.qrp-tomography-parameter-counts-reservoi: Results p.5: the 13 and 45 counts are the paper's own count and the feature-count condition is standard linear algebra, but the 'four- and nine-mode minimum' comes from 'known results [10]' and the SI. Not proved in this paper.
theory_low.casas-multiunitary-condition-for-ame: Sec. III, p.4: the reduced matrices of Eq. (8) are stated with 'it can be shown', with no derivation, and the '2-unitary' term is cited from [7, 21]. The paper states the condition but does not prove it.
theory_low.casas-general-circuit-clifford-except-di: Sec. III.B, pp.5-6: existence of the needed biunimodular vectors for d >= 3 is cited from Ref. [24]. The non-stabilizer consequence is asserted, not proved. The Clifford remark describes their circuit.
theory_low.casas-diagonal-gate-decomposition-d-cont: Sec. III.B, p.6: a proposed decomposition and a claim that general diagonal gates are costly. A construction not tested on hardware; the cost remark is the authors' claim.
theory_low.casas-ame44-eight-qubit-circuit: Sec. III.C.1, pp.6-8: an explicit vector (Eq. 23) and a circuit are given, but multi-unitarity is only 'verified by direct computation' with no proof or shown check. The authors' computational claim, not a proved result.
theory_low.casas-ame46-construction-mixed-qubit-qut: Sec. III.C.2 and App. C: a numerical construction (iterative algorithm of Ref. [24]) with no hardware test, and the depth reduction is left as future work.
theory_low.casas-ame48-twelve-qubit-circuit: Sec. III.C.3 and App. D: a numerically found vector and a Qiskit decomposition. Multi-unitarity is stated, not proved; no hardware test.
theory_low.casas-lu-inequivalence-claim: Appendix A and Sec. III.C.3: a computed result. Table I values are lost in the text layer, and the d = 6 case is not discussed in the Appendix A text. The d = 4 graph versus minimal support case needs a higher moment that is not shown.
theory_low.casas-lu-invariant-second-moment-criteri: Appendix A, p.14: invariance of the spectrum of I(U) is 'easy to verify' and 'it can be shown', with no proof in the paper; the invariants come from Ref. [30]. Note the text layer prints the first 'not equal' as '='.
theory_low.casas-theorem-1-genuine-entanglement-thr: Theorem 1, p.9 (checked on the PDF): F_exp >= (d-1)/d, giving 5/6 for d = 6. The proof in App. E is an outline based on Theorem 1 of Ref. [40], and its last line (E5) prints F_exp >= d/(d-1), which exceeds 1 and contradicts (30). The value omits the formula. Not a complete proof in this paper.
theory_low.casas-appendix-e-proof-outline: App. E, pp.16-18: an outline based on Theorem 1 of Ref. [40] ('we provide an estimation'). It uses a rank-bound (E3, E4) taken from the reference, and the closing line (E5) is misprinted as d/(d-1). Not a full proof.
theory_low.casas-ame46-negativity-vs-noise-28-perce: Sec. IV.C, pp.10-11, Fig. 7: a computed comparison for one state and one noise model; the authors also note GHZ and CUE states are more robust near the maximally mixed state.
theory_low.casas-gate-noise-assumptions-4-percent: Sec. IV.C, p.11: an estimate that rests on three stated assumptions (F6 and P gates much less noisy, Bell preparation noise-free, additive noise). Not a measurement or a proof.
theory_low.casas-teleport-noise: Sec. IV.D, pp.11-12 and Fig. 8: about 35% in the text and 12/35 ~ 34% for AME(4,6) in the caption, beating 2/3. The value matches. A computed result built on a cited fidelity formula [43]; only the AME(4,6) figure is given.
